questions.question: In which of the following cases is a member of the State Legislature NOT required to vacate his/her seat?

options.text: Absence for a week without permission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Absence for a week without permission**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A member of the** State Legislature is not required to vacate their seat in the case of** "Absence for a week without permission";

 
 
• therefore, option 3 is the correct answer. 
 
• However, if a member is absent **for 60 days or more** without permission, the seat is declared vacant (Article 190(4)).
 
 
 
• While a short absence without permission might not automatically vacate a seat,
 
• **It prolonged absences without authorization** can lead to actions being taken to declare the seat vacant depending on the specific rules of the legislative body. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disqualification****​**

 
 
• A member is required to vacate their seat if disqualified. Disqualification can occur due to various reasons such as:
 
 
• Holding an office of profit.
 
• Being of unsound mind or undischarged insolvent.
 
• Not being a citizen of India.
 
• Violating the provisions of the Anti-Defection Law.
 
• **(Relevant Articles: 190(3), 191, and the 10th Schedule of the Constitution)**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Double Membership**​
 
 
• If a person is elected to **both the Parliament and a State Legislature**, or to **two seats in the same house** of the legislature, they cannot retain both positions.
 
• They must **resign from one seat**, or one seat will be vacated automatically as per law.

 **(Relevant Articles: 101 and 190 of the Constitution)**
 
 
 
• **Resignation****​**
 
 
• A member can resign from their position by submitting a resignation to the Speaker (for the Legislative Assembly) or the Chairman (for the Legislative Council).
 
• Once the resignation is accepted, the seat becomes vacant.

 **(Relevant Article: 190(3)(b))**

questions.question: The ‘Kachin Manaw Festival’ is associated with which of the following countries?

• This festival is a significant cultural event for the Kachin people, one of the major ethnic groups in Myanmar.
 
• The **festival features traditional dances, music, and rituals**, and it is a time for the Kachin community to come together and celebrate their heritage.
 
• The Kachin Manaw Festival **usually takes place in January** and is marked by vibrant festivities and communal harmony.

• **Myanmar, formerly known as Burma,** is a country in Southeast Asia bordered by India, Bangladesh, China, Laos, and Thailand.
 
• The **country has a rich cultural heritage with over 135 distinct ethnic groups,** each with its own traditions and festivals.
 
• The Kachin people primarily inhabit the Kachin State in northern Myanmar,** which is known for its mountainous terrain and rich natural resources.**
 
• The Kachin Manaw Festival is one of the most important cultural celebrations for the Kachin people and attracts visitors from across the country and beyond.
 
• Myanmar's diverse cultural landscape includes a variety of other festivals such as the Thingyan Water Festival, the Tazaungdaing Festival of Lights, and the Thadingyut Festival.

questions.question: Meenakshisundaram Pillai, a dance guru from the village of Pandanallur, was famous for which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meenakshisundaram Pillai **was widely recognised for **Bharatnatyam, **which is a classical dance form originating from** Tamil Nadu, India.**
 
• He was a** descendant of the Thanjavur Quartet, **a group of four brothers who were court composers in the early 19th century. 
 
• He trained many famous Bharatanatyam dancers,** including Devadasis like Pandanallur Jayalakshmi and Thangachi Ammal. **
 
• He also trained other dancers, including **Mrinalini Sarabhai, Rukmini Devi, and Tara Chaudhri. **
 
• Pillai's son-in-law, Chokkalingam Pillai, became the doyen Guru of the Pandanallur style after him
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is known for its **intricate footwork, hand gestures, facial expressions** and body movements that narrate a story or convey a message.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam****​**

 
 
• Mohiniyattam is one of the two classical dance forms that originated in Kerala, the other one being Kathakali.
 
• Mohiniyattam gets its name from the word ‘Mohini’, the feminine form of Lord Vishnu, the word means ‘dance of Mohini’.
 
• Dr. Sunanda Nair became the first in India to acquire a Master’s degree in Mohiniyattam. She completed her Ph.D. thesis in Intrinsic Lyrical Feminism in Mohiniyattam from Mumbai University.
 
• Mohiniyattam is based on Natya Shastra’s lasya style. 
 
• It has delicate movements and more feminine facial expressions.
 
• The movements are gentle and glide-like. They do not have terse rhythmic steps. 
 
• More emphasis is on the facial expressions and hand gestures
 
 
 
• **Odissi **
 
 
• Odissi, **a renowned classical dance form of India**, hails from the beautiful state of Odisha.
 
• Known for its sensuousness and lyrical beauty, this dance form, often depicted as a dance of love, seamlessly blends the human and divine aspects of life.
 
• It beautifully captures the subtle nuances of life, as well as the everyday mundane.
 
• The **origins of Odissi can be traced back to an early dance style known as Odhra Magadha.**
 
• This style is referred to as the southeastern style of classical dance in the Natya Shastra, which describes various dance forms.

questions.question: Article 32 of the Constitution of India deals with _________ .

options.text: the Right to Freedom and Religion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Constitutional Remedies**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It is one of the fundamental rights listed in the Constitution that each citizen is entitled to.
 
• It entitles the citizens of India to move the** Supreme Court or High Courts **for the enforcement of these rights.
 
• In the Constituent Assembly debate,** Dr. B.R Ambedkar** said that **Article 32 **is the** heart and soul of the Constitution**.
 
• **Article 32 **falls under **Part III **of the Constitution which includes the fundamental rights of individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The study of cell structure is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** cytology**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytology is the study of individual cells of the body, in contrast to histology which is the study of whole human tissue**.

 
 
• The human body is made up of millions of cells and these can be sampled and viewed under a microscope after appropriate preparation to help diagnose medical conditions.
 
• This involves looking at individual cells for abnormal changes in both the nucleus and the cytoplasm (body) of the cell.
 
• The nucleus contains the genetic material that controls the cell and determines what type of cell it will become, but also controls its behavior.
 
• Cytology is widely used in medicine for the prevention and diagnosis of disease.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Hooke was the first scientist to use the word 'cell' in 1665** when he looked at slices of cork through a lit compound microscope and observed very small, irregular boxes that reminded him of tiny rooms, or cells.

 
 
• Hooke wrote about his findings and drew the structures he saw in his book Micrographia, which was published in 1665.
 
 
 
• The earliest cell theory was developed in 1838 by plant scientist Matthias Schleiden and animal scientist **Theodor Schwann.**
 
• They each came to the same conclusion that the living things they studied were composed of cells.

• The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and other members are the Union State Minister of Revenue or Finance and Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation of all the States.

• Its provisions:
 
 
• Central GST to cover Excise duty, Service tax, etc, State GST to cover VAT, luxury tax, etc.
 
• Integrated GST to cover inter-state trade. IGST per se is not a tax but a system to coordinate state and union taxes.

• Excise duty is a form of tax imposed on goods for their production, licensing, and sale.
 
• Today, excise duty applies only to petroleum and liquor.
 
• Excise duty was levied on manufactured goods and levied at the time of removal of goods, while GST is levied on the supply of goods and services.
 
 
 
• Value Added Tax :
 
 
• Value-added tax (VAT) is a type of indirect tax levied on goods and services for value-added at every point of production or distribution cycle, starting from raw materials and going all the way to the final retail purchase.
 
• Because the consumer bears the entire tax, VAT is also a consumption tax.
 
 
 
• Service Tax :
 
 
• Service tax is a tax levied by the government on service providers on certain service transactions but is actually borne by the customers.
 
• It is categorized under Indirect Tax and came into existence under the Finance Act, 1994.
 
• This tax is not applicable in the state of Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.question:
Identify the correct statements about Independence Day and Republic Day of India.

i) Independence Day is celebrated on 15th August since 1947.

ii) Republic Day is celebrated on 26th January since 1950.

iii) Independence Day is celebrated as Independence from British rule.

iv) Republic day is celebrated since the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Constitution of India in 1949.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** i,ii and iii**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• i**) Independence Day is celebrated on 15th August since 1947.**

 
 
• **This statement is True**
 
• Independence Day marks the day India gained independence from **British rule on 15th August 1947.**
 
• The British ended their colonial rule, and India became an independent nation on that day.
 
• The **first Independence Day was celebrated in 1947, **and since then, it has been celebrated annually on the same date.
 
 
 
• ii) **Republic Day is celebrated on 26th January since 1950**.
 
 
• **This statement is Tru**e
 
• Republic Day is celebrated to honor the date when the **Constitution of India came into effect on 26th January 1950,** making India a Republic.
 
• The day marks the transition from a British Dominion to a fully sovereign nation, where the Indian Constitution became the supreme law of the land.
 
• Even though the **Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949, it was only enforced on 26th January 1950**, which is why Republic Day is celebrated on this date.
 
 
 
• iii) **Independence Day is celebrated as Independence from British rule**.
 
 
• **This statement is True**
 
• Independence Day is a celebration of India's freedom from British colonial rule.
 
• After **nearly 200 years of British contro**l, India gained its independence on 15th August 1947.
 
• It marks the **end of British rule and the beginning of self-governance.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• i**v) Republic Day is celebrated since the Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Constitution of India in 1949**.

 
 
• This statement is not true
 
• The Constituent Assembly did adopt the Constitution on 26th November 1949,** but Republic Day is celebrated on 26th January, the day in 1950** when the Constitution was implemented and India officially became a Republic.
 
• While the Constitution was adopted in 1949, it only came into effect on 26th January 1950, and that's why Republic Day is celebrated on that date.

• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added 10 Fundamental Duties to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 later added the 11th fundamental duty to the list.
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee suggested the adoption of Fundamental Duties in 1976 after they were deemed necessary amid the internal problems of 1975–1977.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are covered by Article 51A of Part-IV A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The basic requirements imposed by the 42nd Amendment Act of the Constitution in 1976 offer the legislature more ability to uphold these commitments in regard to the fundamental rights, in addition to promoting and producing culture.

• They serve as a reminder to Indian citizens of their obligations to society, their fellow citizens, and the country.
 
• They caution people to avoid engaging in anti-social and anti-national behavior.
 
• They motivate others and instill a sense of devotion and discipline in them.
 
• They assist the courts in reviewing and determining whether the statute is constitutional.
 
 
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties:
 
 
• ​To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• To develop scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
• To provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002)

• **The primary source of antioxidants is **typically plant-based foods like fruits, vegetables, and nuts
 
• Antioxidants neutralize** free radicals, preventing damage to cellular function**s
 
• They are believed to **help delay the aging process by reducing oxidative stress. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**
